# Summary of Information on Philip Rubin
Philip Rubin is a multidisciplinary researcher known for his comprehensive work in speech and language sciences, combining computational, engineering, linguistic, physiological, and psychological approaches, with an emphasis on embodied cognition and the biological bases of speech. Beginning in the 1970s at Haskins Laboratories, Rubin contributed foundational developments in speech technology, including the design of computational models and software such as ASY (articulatory synthesis program) and SWS (sinewave synthesis program). His work advanced articulatory phonology and gestural models of speech production and perception, integrating dynamic systems theories and emphasizing the spatiotemporal coordination of global speech attributes. Rubin's innovations have been influential in perceptual organization, multimodal speech processing, and biomechanical modeling of speech articulation.
Beyond research, Rubin has served in significant leadership and policy roles, including directing the Division of Behavioral and Cognitive Sciences at the National Science Foundation, helping launch pivotal programs in cognitive neuroscience and language documentation, and serving as Assistant Director for Social, Behavioral, and Economic Sciences at the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy. His advocacy extends to ethical considerations in research involving human subjects, overseeing standards and participating in interagency committees. Rubin has also been active in science policy, education, and technological ethics, contributing to advisory boards and national panels. Recognized by numerous fellowships and awards, he continues to influence both scientific inquiry and science policy.
